newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Bankovni Holding to raise capital.
newsitem.headline: Czech Bankovni Holding to raise capital.

text.p: Shareholders of Czech investment company Bankovni Holding a.s. voted to increase basic capital by two billion crowns to 3.33 billion in a two-round issue, bank IPB a.s. said on Thursday.
IPB, which is due for further privatisation soon, said in a statement that along with its subsidiary Domeana s.r.o. it holds 54 percent in Bankovni.

IPB said that the first round of the expansion would be a one-for-one rights issue at 1,600 crowns for every share with a 1,000 crown nominal value. Shares unsubscribed in the first round would then be publicly offered at the same price.
The state holds 31.5 percent in the bank, which was approved for further privatisation on Wednesday.
The cabinet charged Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik with drawing up a list of criteria to choose a foreign strategic partner to buy at least part of the state's stake.
Japan's Nomura has said it was interested in the stake. Dutch banks ING Bank NV and ABN AMRO Bank NV are also said to be interested.
IPB said it had offered to buy out minority shareholders of Bankovni Holding. Bankovni has almost 100,000 small shareholders whose combined holdings are around 10 percent of the firm.

Bankovni Holding used to be an investment fund managed by IPB's investment arm Prvni Investicni a.s. before it transformed itself into a holding company earlier this year when stricter regulations on investment funds took effect.
